Poached Irish Salmon

Served at: Feast of St. Muirgen (Lí Ban the Mermaid)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 20 min

Poached Irish Salmon is a delicate and traditional dish often served during the Feast of St. Muirgen, also known as the celebration of Lí Ban the Mermaid. This dish honors the legend of Lí Ban, who was transformed into a mermaid, by featuring fresh salmon from Irish waters, symbolizing the sea and its bounty.

Ingredients

  • 4 salmon fillets (6 oz / 170 g each), skin on
  • 4 cups (1 L) water
  • 1 cup (240 ml) dry white wine
  • 1 lemon, sliced
  • 1 small onion, thinly sliced
  • 2 sprigs fresh dill
  • 2 sprigs fresh parsley
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 teaspoon black peppercorns
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
  • Fresh dill sprigs, for garnish

Method

  1. In a large, deep skillet or saucepan, combine water, white wine, lemon slices, onion, dill, parsley, bay leaf, peppercorns, and salt.
  2. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce heat to low to maintain a gentle poach.
  3. Add the salmon fillets skin side down to the simmering liquid, ensuring they are fully submerged.
  4. Poach the salmon gently for about 12-15 minutes, or until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
  5. Carefully remove the salmon from the liquid using a slotted spatula and place on a serving platter.
  6. Dot the salmon with unsalted butter and garnish with fresh dill sprigs before serving.

Tips

  • Use fresh, high-quality salmon for the best flavor and texture.
  • Do not let the poaching liquid boil, as this will toughen the salmon.
  • Serve with boiled new potatoes and steamed greens for a traditional Irish meal.
